A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forward game-tree model and complexity analyses. The text, equations, algorithms, five figures, and Appendices A–C support a complete comparison. v2 additionally contains expanded discussion and a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: Appendix B reports original Monte Carlo simulations validating TEST, ALPHA-BETA, and SCOUT complexity equations, with results averaged over five independent seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Monte Carlo simulation results in Appendix B, Figures 3–5, including seed averages and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: The forward sampler and Algorithms 1–5 retain the same procedures, including special-child selection, conditional sampling, pruning, and threshold updates. Expanded explanations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic game-tree scenarios using uniform, triangular, cubic power, and bimodal-uniform distributions. No additional task, domain, or input scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains ALPHA-BETA, SCOUT, TEST-BRUTEFORCE, TEST-BISECTION, and TEST-HARDEST. Expanded discussion of MCTS, PVS, and MTD(f) does not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figure 2 retains its parameter settings, including b = 10 and n = 5 for the finite-depth comparison, and normalization by average TEST complexity. Appendix B retains the same parameter grids and Monte Carlo trial ranges.

E4.justification: The distribution-dependent complexity comparisons and Appendix B validation against Monte Carlo estimates are retained unchanged. The new limitations discussion introduces no ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent seeds and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals in Appendix B. The new checklist explains why Figure 2's exact expected-value calculations lack sampling error bars, without changing uncertainty reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 contain identical result graphics, including complexity curves, Monte Carlo estimates, and oracle values. ALPHA-BETA's approach toward TEST-BRUTEFORCE and SCOUT's lower deep-tree costs remain the same; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 repairs the marginal TEST-complexity definition: v1 averages a cost indexed by x under a differently named random variable, whereas v2 consistently indexes the cost by the sampled root X. The recurrences, theorem conclusions, and proofs in Appendices A and C otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction shifts from proposing a novel model to specifying and analyzing a simple model, alongside acknowledgment of earlier top-down models. Claims about representing real games are qualified as coarse. The principal complexity and finite-depth performance claims remain intact.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's limitations concerning discrete values and unanalyzed algorithms, v2 Section 8 explicitly disclaims accurate real-game dynamics and discusses constant branching/depth, parent-only homogeneous conditionals, and the particular truncation choice. It also substantially qualifies extrapolation from SCOUT and TEST-BISECTION to PVS and MTD(f).

D1.justification: v1 promises a public repository upon acceptance; v2 supplies a repository address in footnote 3. The existing consumer-grade laptop and CPU-time disclosure remains unchanged. The added checklist mostly restates reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Scheucher–Kaindl, Furtak–Buro, Coquelin–Munos, and Orseau–Munos while retaining the earlier references. Sections 3 and 7 now identify the Prefix Value Game Tree Model as a close predecessor and develop a substantially fuller comparison with prior tree-generation models and MCTS analysis.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title, terminology, and explanatory passages while retaining most of the technical narrative. The combined closing section becomes separate related-work and discussion/limitations sections, followed by broader impact and a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: All five figure graphics remain identical. Figure 2's caption more clearly explains normalized complexity and the multiplicative factor. Publication-header changes and text reflow alter page layout, but the figures and algorithm displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution through its discussion of closely related models, makes applicability boundaries more explicit, and supplies a code-repository address. These changes improve the interpretation and accessibility of the retained analysis. The overall gain is limited: the substantive proofs and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
